scenes.tts: Here is natural selection at four levels.
scenes.narration: Here is natural selection at four levels.
scenes.visual: Heading 'Natural selection' in the title face. The site's ladder, redrawn (upright rails, simplest at the foot, 'Simpler' at the foot, 'Deeper' at the top), empty: four rungs with the level labels only, from the top 'College, the core', 'High school', 'Grade 7', 'Ages 5 to 10'. Hex stands on the High school rung from the first frame and does not move until s06_hop.

scenes.tts: For ages five to ten, a child plays a hungry bird and hunts yarn worms in grass. The green and brown ones are often left.
scenes.caption: For ages 5 to 10, a child plays a hungry bird and hunts yarn worms in grass. The green and brown ones are often left.
scenes.narration: For ages 5 to 10, a child plays a hungry bird and hunts yarn worms in grass. The green and brown ones are often left.
scenes.visual: A thin teal outline marks the Ages 5 to 10 rung; its lesson title 'The Camouflage Hunt' and the note 'Be the hungry bird: which yarn worms get eaten last?' appear on the rung. Beside the ladder: a square of green lawn seen from above with a stick at each corner and 20 short yarn worms on it, 5 each of green, brown, red and yellow, and a small cup at the edge. At 'hunts' the red and yellow worms are lifted into the cup first; the green and brown ones stay in the grass. Tag 'schematic'. No bird is drawn: the child is the bird.

scenes.tts: In grade seven, real counts: dark peppered moths near Cambridge were about twelve percent of those caught in two thousand one, and about one percent in two thousand seven.
scenes.caption: In grade 7, real counts: dark peppered moths near Cambridge were about 12 percent of those caught in 2001, and about 1 percent in 2007.
scenes.narration: In grade 7, real counts: dark peppered moths near Cambridge were about 12 percent of those caught in 2001, and about 1 percent in 2007.
scenes.visual: The outline moves to the Grade 7 rung; title 'Natural Selection in Action' and note 'Hunt moths on clean and sooty bark, then read the real counts.' appear. Beside the ladder two bars: 2001 at 12 percent and 2007 at 1 percent; y-axis 'dark moths, percent of moths caught'; label 'Madingley, near Cambridge, England; light-trap samples'; small print 'values read from a graph, so rounded'. No 2004 point, no arrow of cause.

scenes.tts: In high school, Gorongosa's elephants. Before the war, eighteen point five percent of sampled females had no tusks. Among survivors, fifty point nine. No elephant had to lose her tusks.
scenes.caption: In high school, Gorongosa's elephants. Before the war, 18.5 percent of sampled females had no tusks. Among survivors, 50.9. No elephant had to lose her tusks.
scenes.narration: In high school, Gorongosa's elephants. Before the war, 18.5 percent of sampled females had no tusks. Among survivors, 50.9. No elephant had to lose her tusks.
scenes.visual: The outline moves to the High school rung; title 'Variation and Survival' and note 'Poaching in Gorongosa raised tuskless females from 18.5 to 50.9 percent.' appear. Beside the ladder two rows of simple elephant icons with the tuskless share filled: 'before the war' 18.5 percent (n = 54 females) and 'survivors' 50.9 percent (n = 108 females). At the last sentence one tuskless icon on the 'before' row is tagged 'already tuskless'. No icon ever changes from tusked to tuskless.

scenes.tts: In college, Daphne Major's finches. Survivors of the nineteen seventy-seven drought had larger beaks. That is selection, not yet evolution. A breeder's equation predicts the chicks' average.
scenes.caption: In college, Daphne Major's finches. Survivors of the 1977 drought had larger beaks. That is selection, not yet evolution. A breeder's equation predicts the chicks' average.
scenes.narration: In college, Daphne Major's finches. Survivors of the 1977 drought had larger beaks. That is selection, not yet evolution. A breeder's equation predicts the chicks' average.
scenes.visual: The outline moves to the College, the core rung; title 'How to Test an Evolutionary Explanation' and note 'Daphne Major's 1977 drought shows selection; the breeder's equation predicts the offspring shift.' appear. Beside the ladder two beak outlines without numbers: 'before the drought', a medium beak, and 'survivors', a deeper one (schematic). At 'not yet evolution' the label 'selection' sits on the arrow between them and a second arrow leads to 'chicks?'. At 'A breeder's equation' the chip 'R = h² × S' appears with 'S: how far the survivors' average sits from the population's' and 'R: how far the chicks' average moves'.

scenes.tts: If the elephants lose you, hop down to the moths, then back up.
scenes.narration: If the elephants lose you, hop down to the moths, then back up.
scenes.visual: All four rungs stay with their titles and notes; the outline is gone. The Gorongosa rows and the moth bars are both visible beside the ladder. At 'hop down to the moths' Hex hops down one rung from High school to Grade 7 and lands, one beat still; at 'then back up' Hex hops back to High school. This is the only place in the film where Hex moves.

scenes.tts: A level is a place to start, not a rank.
scenes.narration: A level is a place to start, not a rank.
scenes.visual: The ladder as in the last scene with Hex on High school; beside it the sentence set large: 'A level is a place to start, not a rank.' Hold; no motion. Nothing on the ladder is dimmed.
Standard end card. Line: 'A level is a place to start, not a rank.'
